text: Only to the duration of the data packet, but accounts also for the safe and possible ACK. So, as represented here, BNC will send their nonce counter to a value that covers the all expected duration of the dialogue. I'm saying expected because you don't know if the acknowledgement will be there or not, right? At the beginning, when we read this field here, the packet might be successful or not, we don't know. If it fails, the ACK will not be there, right? If it's successful, we do have ACK. But what we expect, we are optimistic. What we expect is that the acknowledgement will be there. So always, this duration field here for response to the data packet duration plus safe plus acknowledgement, because we account for the expected optimistically expected duration of the data. Now, why do they do that in Wi-Fi? Because they really want to be sure that nobody interrupts a dialogue. Remember, a dialogue is a high priority thing, right? So nobody should interrupt an ongoing dialogue. To make sure that nobody interrupts a dialogue, they added this extra measure of caution. That is.
